b.title: Lessons from Making Dubai Chewy Cookies

content.paragraph1: As a mere beginner, I'd always rely on YouTube tutorials to guide my cooking process. But the thing is, no matter how easy a tutorial can be, I'll always find a way to make it difficult. And perhaps, you've experienced the same thing too.
content.paragraph2: Our little group had just made our first batch of Dubai Chewy Cookies to raise funds for a future donation event. But, making the simple desert proved to be a hectic task.
content.paragraph2.1: We were off to a smooth start by by frying the kataifi, mixing in the pistachio paste, and setting off into the fridge, until we arrived to the melting part. For some reason the marshmallow just wouldn't melt, it clumped together and turn into this charcoal-like dough. I guess that's what we get for using off-looking marshmallows. Well then, it’s time to purchase new bags of marshmallows. Luckily the newly bought marshmallows were melting (as it should) and we added the chocolate powder. Problem one solved; but at the expense of spending more money.
content.paragraph3: Now time to shape the pistachio-kataifi filling. We thought that cooling it in the fridge would hardened it but after a touch we know that was not the case. It was too mushy to be rolled into a ball. We got pistachio-kataifi all over our hands 🙌. After making a huge mess, we finally _ around 28 balls (but a lot of the filling were wasted in the process 😭)
content.paragraph4: But the hardest part had to be wrapping the kunafa filling with the marshmallow. These inexperienced hands weren’t prepared to handle sticky marshmallow skin. We proceeded to make all sorts of wonky shapes. Instead of a smooth rounded ball, we had a humongous flat dripping balls. It was looking hopeless until a helper came into the scene. My mom helped us shaping the Dubai Chewy Cookies; her secret was a bit of oil mixed to the hands. And with that 25 Dubai Chewy Cookies were packaged and ready to be sold.

b.author: Naya Visista Valentine
